messages:
cassandra: Quick thread — POC for a 'shard-consistency-checker' that runs during streaming safetensors loads. It does a cheap header + per-chunk blake3 verify and triggers a fallback full-fetch on mismatch. Thoughts?
ajay: Nice. Question: where does this live — loader or indexer? Doing it in the loader adds latency on hot-path.
cassandra: Plan is hybrid: indexer publishes signed manifest with per-shard checksum and schema_version; loader does a header-level fast-verify (magic + declared sizes) synchronously and schedules an async chunk checksum. If async detect mismatch -> abort and fetch full shard via fallback.
maria: What about partial streams that cut mid-shard? Need a resume/handshake so client can request ranges and server can respond with range validity.
lia: Concern: extra RTT per shard for handshake kills tail latency. Can we piggyback verification in the normal range GET response headers? e.g., server returns X-Shard-Checksum and X-Chunk-Start so loader can verify without extra roundtrip.
ajay: Piggybacking looks best. Loader can speculatively trust first chunk, verify asynchronously, and if mismatch fallback. Need backpressure so we don't feed bad weights into GPU.
cassandra: Example header sketch:```
GET /weights/shard-0001?range=0-65535
-> 200
X-Shard-Checksum: blake3:abcd1234...
X-Chunk-Start: 0
Content-Range: bytes 0-65535/1234567
```
maria: How do we handle retries? If checksum fails after streaming 2MB, we must not use those activations. Evict partials, increment metric "stream-check-fail", and re-fetch shard via full reliable path (non-streaming).
lia: Also expose metrics: stream-check-fail, fallback-full-fetch, handshake-latency, verify-delay. Dashboards should show warmup vs runtime failures.
infra-bot: deploy-notice: canary of shard-consistency-checker landed on hostpool-gpu-2 at 2026-03-01T12:34:00Z
ajay: Edge-case: safetensors may have build-time canonical serialization differences (padding, field order). We must checksum canonical bytes used by the indexer. Add schema_version in manifest to avoid silent mismatch.
cassandra: Agreed — manifest will include schema_version and canonical_size. Loader will detect version skew and fallback to compat loader if needed.
maria: Warmup interaction: warmup prefetches many shards; full checks on every shard would increase bandwidth. Proposal: warmup performs headers-only validation + sampling (verify 1/20 chunks) and first-exec triggers full-check.
lia: Also provide an opt-in fast-path manifest flag for dedicated customers to skip checks (trust_level: high). Document security tradeoffs.
cassandra: Action items: I'll write a short RFC with proto for streaming-handshake + header fields, piggyback vs explicit RTT perf numbers, and a test harness that simulates corrupt shards. Assigning: @ajay for manifest spec, @maria for warmup policy experiments, @lia for diagrams. ETA: EOD Friday.
ajay: I'll sketch manifest fields: [shard_id, size_bytes, blake3_hex, canonical_size, schema_version, trust_level, signed_by].
maria: I'll run a warmup sampling sim and attach numbers to the RFC.
lia: I'll make a diagram of handshake vs piggyback flow for the doc.
cassandra: :thumbsup:
